newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher as mood improves.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher as mood improves.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Wednesday, boosted by an improved mood in the market following disappointment a day earlier over the central bank's decision to leave interest rates unchanged, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.15 percent, or 2.25 points, to 198.07 on an all-share turnover of 62 million shekels against 76 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 1.18 percent to 207.98.

"The market was showing strength today and it looks good. The positive trend started towards the end of Tuesday's trading day when options speculators started pushing the market," said Doron Tzur, head of research at Sahar Securities.

"Other investors followed the options players and the market closed with only mild decline. Prices are very attractive and the earning reports that were published were within expectations," Tzur added.
On Monday, after the market's close, the central bank said it would keep its key lending rate unchanged for December at an annualised 15.2 percent despite demands from industrialists for lower rates.
"The mood in the market has improved. The fact that the market closed on Tuesday with only a mild decline is seen as a very good sign," said Elish Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.
"Foreign investors are more active and portfolio managers are also showing more interest in the market as they try to show improved results before the end of the year," Rosenfeld said.
Koor Industries, the most active share, fell 0.5 percent to 28,092 on volume of 4.3 million shekels after reporting a third-quarter net income of $31.3 million against $34.7 million a year earlier.

Clal Israel rose 1.25 percent to 7,365 after it reported third-quarter net profit of 1.6 million shekels against 72.9 million shekels a year earlier. Traders said the results were within expectations and were reflected in the share's price.
The Israel Corp fell 3.0 percent to 17,444 after reporting a third-quarter net loss of 8.8 million shekels against net profit of 59.5 million shekels a year earlier.

Elbit, plunged the maximum 10.0 percent to 3,560. Elbit said on Monday it had completed its break-up into three publicly traded companies. Traders said the share fell because only the company making non-military electronics was traded in the session. The other two companies, which make military products, will start trading on Thursday.
Bank Leumi rose 1.75 percent to 401 after it said it had completed the sale of a controlling stake in Africa Israel Investments to Israeli businessman Lev Leviev for $190 million.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, the second most active share, gained 3.0 percent to 150,005 on turnover of 2.9 million shekels after its share traded on Nasdaq rose 3.3 percent on Tuesday.
Clal Industries rose 2.0 percent to 1,373 on a volume of 2.0 million shekels.
